newEntriesNeeded.title: COLL ALL PML1 declarative collection query
newEntriesNeeded.principle: COLL ALL is the PML1 declarative syntax for querying all elements of a given type from the database, with optional WITH clause for filtering.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use COLL ALL (TYPE) WITH (conditions) to build a collection variable. Compound conditions use eq, neq, inset, NOT, EMPTY, ISNAMED, etc.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax: var !varName COLL ALL (ElementType) WITH (:Attr1 eq |value1| and :Attr2 neq |value2|)
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
var !tags COLL ALL (ENGITEM) WITH (:TagStatus eq |ACTIVE| and ISNAMED and NOT(EMPTY(:RAMTAGOWNER)) and :RAMTAGOWNER eq |LEIR|)
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern: var !tags = !!collectallfor('engitem', '|ACTIVE|', !!ce)  -- PML2 procedural form, different semantics
pitfalls: COLL ALL returns STRING array of element references, not DBREF objects
Each element in the result is a STRING that must be converted via .dbref()
The WITH clause uses PML1 attribute syntax (:AttrName)

newEntriesNeeded.title: do ... values loop for array iteration
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The 'do ... values' construct iterates over each element value in an array, assigning the value to the loop variable.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use 'do !var values !array' to iterate over array values. This is the idiomatic PML loop for iterating array elements by value (not index).
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
do !i from 1 to !tags.size()
    !tagString = !tags[!i]  -- index-based, less idiomatic
enddo
pitfalls: Loop variable is a STRING copy, not a reference
Cannot modify the original array from within the loop
Nested with do ... from ... to requires careful index management

newEntriesNeeded.title: inset() string containment function
newEntriesNeeded.principle: inset() checks whether a string value is contained in a list of string values.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use inset(string, |val1|, |val2|, ...) to test if the string matches any of the listed values. Returns TRUE or FALSE.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
LOWCASE(:TagClassName) inset(|gas detector|, |heat detector|, |junction box|)
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern: :TagClassName eq |gas detector| or :TagClassName eq |heat detector|  -- verbose equivalent
pitfalls: inset() is case-sensitive; use LOWCASE() or UPCASE() for case-insensitive matching
Only available in PML1 WITH clause expressions

newEntriesNeeded.title: IFT() conditional function
newEntriesNeeded.principle: IFT() is a PML inline conditional function: IFT(condition, trueValue, falseValue).
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use IFT(test, valueIfTrue, valueIfFalse) for inline conditional logic in expressions.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
if (!condition) then
    !result = |true_val|
else
    !result = |false_val|
endif  -- longer form
pitfalls: All three arguments are evaluated before the function call — no short-circuit evaluation
Return type is ANY; may need explicit type handling

newEntriesNeeded.title: BLOCK object with evaluate() for dynamic PML expressions
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The BLOCK object wraps a PML expression string and can be evaluated against a DBREF to produce a runtime value.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use 'object BLOCK(expressionString)' to create a block, then 'dbref.evaluate(block)' to compute the result.
pitfalls: Expression string must be valid PML syntax
Handle exceptions with handle ANY around evaluate() call
Returns ANY type; may be STRING, REAL, or ERROR

newEntriesNeeded.title: NETGRIDCONTROL object methods: clearGrid, BindToDataSource, saveGridToExcel
newEntriesNeeded.principle: NETGRIDCONTROL is a .NET add-in object for displaying tabular data in PML. Key methods include clearGrid(), BindToDataSource(), and saveGridToExcel().
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Create NETGRIDCONTROL, clearGrid(), bind NETDATASOURCE, then optionally saveGridToExcel() for export.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
!grid = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!grid.clearGrid()
!source = object NETDATASOURCE(label, headers, data)
!grid.BindToDataSource(!source)
!grid.saveGridToExcel(path)
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern: !grid = object array()  -- ARRAY is not NETGRIDCONTROL
pitfalls: Requires 'import GridControl' and 'using namespace |Aveva.Core.Presentation|'
NETDATASOURCE label parameter is a string identifier
saveGridToExcel() path must be a valid file path string

newEntriesNeeded.title: OBJECT DATETIME() constructor and accessor methods
newEntriesNeeded.principle: OBJECT DATETIME() creates a datetime object. Access year, month, date, hour, minute via accessor methods.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use !dt = OBJECT DATETIME() then !dt.year(), !dt.month(), etc. Convert to formatted string with .string('format').
pitfalls: .string('I2') pads with leading zero for single-digit months/days/hours
Available as PML2 object; verify PML1 equivalent if needed

newEntriesNeeded.title: Nested handle ANY inside do loops for per-iteration error recovery
newEntriesNeeded.principle: A handle ANY block can be nested inside a do loop to catch and recover from errors per-iteration without aborting the entire loop.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Wrap per-iteration risky operations in handle ANY. Set fallback values in the handler. Use endhandle to close the block.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
do !i values !array
    handle any
        !result = |fallback value|
    endhandle
enddo
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- mac_36
if (!expression.unset().not() or !expression.empty().not()) then
    !block = object BLOCK(!expression)
    !value = !tagRef.evaluate(!block)
    handle any
        !value = 'Error when calculating value as per expression [$!attributeEntry.:RDLDabaconExpression] for element [$!tagRef.name]. Error: $!!error.text'
    endhandle
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
handle any
    do !i values !array
        -- entire loop in one handler
    enddo
endhandle  -- catches too broadly
pitfalls: Nested handle ANY inside outer handle ANY requires careful scoping
!!error.text is available only within the handler block
Always set a fallback value in the handler to avoid UNSET propagation
